newsitem.title: CHINA: China official says no freeze on red-chip listings.
newsitem.headline: China official says no freeze on red-chip listings.

text.p: Chinese officials denied on Thursday they had imposed a freeze on new listings of red-chip companies until after a crucial Communist Party meeting later this year, but said tighter checks were being imposed.
"There has been no suspension, we just want to carry out more rigorous checks before giving approvals to firms to list shares abroad," an official of the State Administration of State Property said.
"We aim to further regulate the process," she said, but gave no details.

The Hong Kong Economic Times reported that the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) would not give approval for any red-chip listings until after the 15th party congress, expected to take place in late September or in October.

Red chips are Hong Kong-based companies with Chinese mainland financial backing. At least 14 municipal and provincial governments in China were preparing to seek listings for their window companies in Hong Kong, the newspaper said.
A CSRC official who declined to be identified, said he had no knowledge of such a freeze and that no such document had been issued.
"We know nothing about it," a CSRC spokesman said. "If we have something to announce, we will make a formal statement just as we did before."

The property administration official said no action to curb listings of red chips had been taken since late June when the State Council, or cabinet, announced that all Chinese-controlled companies making offers abroad must first obtain approval from domestic regulators.
Preparations for more listings were going ahead, the property administration official said, but gave no timetable.
"More firms are preparing for listings in Hong Kong as red chips," she said. "We are still receiving applications from firms and we are continuing to process them."

She reiterated details of the State Council directive, saying firms wanting to list shares abroad would have to obtain approval from the CSRC, the State Administration of State Property and the State Economic and Trade Commission.
"Firms cannot float shares abroad without permission from the authorities," she said.
"There have been serious irregularities in the past," she said, adding that for a company to be selected for listing it must meet requirements.

Red chips have become the hottest shares on Hong Kong's stock market in recent months, with much of the excitement generated by expectations of asset injections into the company by a mainland corporate parent after the listing.
